body.statement:
There is a single jointly Borel-measurable implementation of \(\mathrm{def:implementation\text{-}handle}\) that obeys the fixed arm-within-stratum coordinate order, uses parent-only recursion, selects the lexicographically first retained child, and tests separately every closed child containing a shared-boundary point.  For every fixed \(C_v<\infty\) and depth \(k\), uniformly over \(h\in\mathcal H\) and \(\lVert v\rVert\le C_v\) in the local fiber, its selected ambient boxes and feasible cells equal \(\mathcal D_j^\dagger\) and \(\mathcal C_j^\dagger\), respectively, for all \(j\le k\), with probability tending to one.  If \(\gamma_j(L)\) is the positive population separation at depth \(j\) defined in the proof, the deterministic depth \(j_n(L)\) obtained by comparing the pilot approximation envelope with \(\gamma_1(L),\ldots,\gamma_{j_n(L)}(L)\) tends to infinity.  The decreasing envelope
\[
a_n(L)=\sup_{m\ge n}2^{-j_m(L)}
\]
therefore tends to zero and satisfies
\[
\lVert\widehat r_n-r^\dagger\rVert=O_P\{a_n(L)\}
\]
locally uniformly on every fixed bounded nuisance fiber.  The conclusion holds for disconnected, flat, tied, and dyadic-boundary minimizing sets, and every positive prefix separation has an eventually positive outward certificate on effectively represented instances.  A jointly measurable, slowly refining rectangle-constant Gaussian rule applied to \(\sqrt n\,\widetilde\theta_n\) has data-to-Gaussian risk error \(o(1)\) uniformly on every such fiber and obeys
\[
\limsup_{n\to\infty}\ \sup_{h\in\mathcal H,\,\lVert v\rVert\le C_v}
E\!\left[\sum_{j=1}^{M}\delta_{n,j}(\sqrt n\,\widetilde\theta_n)
\ell_{\mathrm{reg}}(h,j)\right]\le V^*.
\]
No objective-uniform spatial rate follows from continuity and uniform objective-approximation error alone: for every \(\epsilon>0\), the two continuous objectives \(f_+(z)=\epsilon z\) and \(f_-(z)=\epsilon(1-z)\) on \([0,1]\) have canonical minimizers separated by one, while the common approximation \(g(z)=\epsilon/2\) is within \(\epsilon/2\) of each in supremum norm.  This is a generic continuous-objective obstruction only; it proves no model-specific lower rate for the Gaussian-risk family \(r\mapsto L(r)\).
body.proof_tex:
Write \(c_{ax}=p_xe_{ax}\).  The stipulated spaces of \(p\) and \(e\) give
\[
c_{ax}>0,\qquad \sum_{a,x}c_{ax}=1,
\tag{1}
\]
and feasibility gives \(\rho\le r_{ax}\le1\).  Choose two distinct support values \(y_u\ne y_w\), which exist because the \(L\) support values are distinct and \(L\ge3\).  For every probability vector \(q_c\) in a cell \(c=(a,x)\), direct expansion around its mean gives
\[
\sigma_c^2(q_c)
=\frac12\sum_{\ell,m}q_{c\ell}q_{cm}(y_\ell-y_m)^2
=\sum_{\ell<m}q_{c\ell}q_{cm}(y_\ell-y_m)^2.
\tag{2}
\]
By \(\mathrm{ass:eta\text{-}interior}\), (2) at \(q^0\) implies
\[
\underline\sigma^2:=\eta^2(y_u-y_w)^2
\le \sigma_{ax}^2(q^0)\le4C_Y^2=:\overline\sigma^2.
\tag{3}
\]
The upper bound uses \(\lvert Y-\mu_{ax}\rvert\le2C_Y\).  Since \(F=[d_1\ \cdots\ d_K]\operatorname{diag}(p)\), the positivity of every \(p_x\) and \(\operatorname{rank}(F)=d\) from \(\mathrm{ass:menu\text{-}rank}\) imply that \(d_1,\ldots,d_K\) span \(\mathbb R^d\).  Hence
\[
\lambda_D:=\min_{\lVert u\rVert_2=1}\sum_{x=1}^K(u^\top d_x)^2>0.
\tag{4}
\]
Equations (1)--(4), the annotation floor, and the displayed formula for \(\Sigma(r)\) yield constants \(0<\lambda_-\le\lambda_+<\infty\), depending only on the fixed problem, such that
\[
\lambda_-I_d\preceq\Sigma(r)\preceq\lambda_+I_d
\quad\text{for every }r\in\mathcal R_B.
\tag{5}
\]
For example, the lower bound follows from
\[
u^\top\Sigma(r)u
=\sum_{x,a}\frac{p_x\sigma_{ax}^2(q^0)}{e_{ax}r_{ax}}(u^\top d_x)^2
\ge \underline\sigma^2\min_xp_x\sum_x(u^\top d_x)^2,
\]
because \(e_{ax}r_{ax}\le1\); the upper bound follows from \(e_{ax}r_{ax}\ge\rho\min_{a,x}e_{ax}>0\).  Thus every inversion and Gaussian comparison below takes place in one compact positive-definite covariance set.

We next construct the pilot objective and quantify its error.  For pilot record \(i\), let
\[
U_{i,ax\ell}=\mathbf 1\{X_i=x,A_i=a,Y_i=y_\ell\},
\qquad V_{i,ax}=\mathbf 1\{X_i=x,A_i=a\}.
\]
The pilot is fully annotated and independent of the main wave.  Under \(q_n(h,v)\),
\[
E U_{i,ax\ell}=c_{ax}q_{n,ax\ell}(h,v),
\qquad E V_{i,ax}=c_{ax}.
\tag{6}
\]
Define the raw conditional-frequency estimator as the ratio of the corresponding pilot averages when its denominator is positive, and arbitrarily otherwise.  Project each resulting cell vector in Euclidean norm onto
\[
\mathcal Q_\eta=\left\{u\in\mathbb R^L:u_\ell\ge\eta,
\ \sum_{\ell=1}^Lu_\ell=1\right\};
\]
call the projected array \(\widehat q_n\).  This projection is unique and nonexpansive because \(\mathcal Q_\eta\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, and \(q^0_c\in\mathcal Q_\eta\) by \(\mathrm{def:saturated\text{-}model}\).

Put
\[
b_n=\left\{\frac{\log(n+1)}{m_n}\right\}^{1/2},
\qquad t_n=b_n^{1/2}.
\tag{7}
\]
Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:pilot\text{-}rate}\) gives \(m_n\to\infty\) and \(\log(n+1)/m_n\to0\), so \(b_n\to0\) and \(b_n=o(t_n)\).  Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:pilot\text{-}vanishes}\) also gives
\[
\frac{n^{-1/2}}{b_n}
=\left\{\frac{m_n}{n\log(n+1)}\right\}^{1/2}\longrightarrow0.
\tag{8}
\]
Every variable in (6) is bounded by one.  Chebyshev's inequality at threshold proportional to \(b_n\), followed by a union bound over the fixed \(2KL+2K\) averages, gives a constant \(C_1<\infty\) and events \(E_{n,C_v}\) such that
\[
\sup_{h\in\mathcal H,\,\lVert v\rVert\le C_v}
P_{q_n(h,v)}(E_{n,C_v}^{c})
\le \frac{C_1}{\log(n+1)}+o(1).
\tag{9}
\]
On these events every empirical cell denominator is at least \(c_{ax}/2\) for all sufficiently large \(n\).  The elementary ratio identity
\[
\frac{u}{w}-\frac{u_0}{w_0}
=\frac{u-u_0}{w}+\frac{u_0(w_0-w)}{ww_0}
\tag{10}
\]
and \(\min_{a,x}c_{ax}>0\) then bound every raw conditional-frequency error by a fixed multiple of \(b_n\).  The compactness conclusion in \(\mathrm{thm:local\text{-}chart\text{-}membership}\) gives, for fixed \(C_v\),
\[
\sup_{h\in\mathcal H,\,\lVert v\rVert\le C_v}
\lVert q_n(h,v)-q^0\rVert_\infty=O(n^{-1/2}).
\tag{11}
\]
Combining (8)--(11) with nonexpansiveness of projection shows that, on \(E_{n,C_v}\) and eventually for each fixed \(C_v\),
\[
\lVert\widehat q_n-q^0\rVert_\infty\le C_2b_n.
\tag{12}
\]
The constant in (12) can be fixed independently of \(C_v\): the \(C_v\)-dependent constant multiplying \(n^{-1/2}\) in (11) is eventually absorbed by (8).  The same argument, using the fully labelled pilot cell means and their stipulated clipping, gives
\[
\max_{a,x}\lvert\widehat\beta_{ax}-\mu_{ax}(q_n(h,v))\rvert
=O_P(b_n)
\tag{13}
\]
locally uniformly on the bounded fiber.

Let \(\widehat\sigma_{n,ax}^2\) be the variance of \(\mathcal Y\) under \(\widehat q_{n,ax}\), and define
\[
\widehat\Sigma_n(r)
=\sum_{x,a}\frac{p_x\widehat\sigma_{n,ax}^2}{e_{ax}r_{ax}}d_xd_x^\top.
\tag{14}
\]
The variance is a polynomial in the cell probabilities on the compact simplex, so (12), \(r_{ax}\ge\rho\), and the finiteness of the index set imply
\[
\sup_{r\in\mathcal R_B}
\lVert\widehat\Sigma_n(r)-\Sigma(r)\rVert_F\le C_3b_n
\quad\text{on }E_{n,C_v}.
\tag{15}
\]
Moreover, (2) applies to \(\widehat q_n\in\mathcal Q_\eta\), so the covariance matrices in (14) obey the same kind of positive lower and finite upper bounds as (5).

For clarity, we derive rather than assume the covariance modulus used next.  If \(S_t=S+t(T-S)\) stays in a compact subset of \(\mathbb S_{++}^d\), differentiation of the normal density gives
\[
\frac{d}{dt}\phi_{S_t}(z-h)
=\frac12\phi_{S_t}(z-h)
\left\{(z-h)^\top S_t^{-1}(T-S)S_t^{-1}(z-h)
-\operatorname{tr}(S_t^{-1}(T-S))\right\}.
\tag{16}
\]
The Gaussian second-moment identity and the uniform bounds on \(S_t^{-1}\) show, after integrating the absolute value in (16), that
\[
\int_{\mathbb R^d}\lvert\phi_T(z-h)-\phi_S(z-h)\rvert\,dz
\le C_4\lVert T-S\rVert_F,
\tag{17}
\]
uniformly in \(h\).  Let
\[
R_H=2\max_{h\in\mathcal H}\lVert h\rVert_\infty<\infty.
\tag{18}
\]
The regret of every randomized rule lies in \([0,R_H]\).  Thus (17) bounds the difference between its risks under the two covariances by \(R_HC_4\lVert T-S\rVert_F/2\).  Taking first the supremum over \(h\) and then the infimum over rules preserves this bound.  If \(\widehat L_n\) denotes the Gaussian game value with covariance (14), (15) therefore proves
\[
\sup_{r\in\mathcal R_B}\lvert\widehat L_n(r)-L(r)\rvert
\le C_5b_n
\quad\text{on }E_{n,C_v}.
\tag{19}
\]

We now specify the measurable nested-cell sieve.  Let
\[
k_n=\left\lfloor\log_2\log(n+2)\right\rfloor.
\tag{20}
\]
At each depth at most \(k_n\), and only among the closed feasible children of the currently selected ambient parent, compute the minimum of \(\widehat L_n\) to deterministic absolute error at most \(b_n\).  Denote the resulting approximation for child \(b\) at depth \(j\) by \(\widehat v_{n,j,b}\).  On represented inputs, repeat the finite-grid construction certified by \(\mathrm{thm:certified\text{-}computation}\) with the child's finitely many dyadic box inequalities adjoined and with algebraic nearest-point projection onto the resulting nonempty compact polytope.  The projection supplies finite algebraic covering nets of that feasible child, and the same state, observation, probability, and primal--dual error bounds certify its restricted minimum.  On a fixed nonrepresented mathematical input, use deterministic successively finer nets of the compact feasible child, together with the same state nets, fixed rational observation rectangles, and successively accurate Gaussian integrals.  The covariance bounds (5), (14), and the modulus (17) make those finite approximations uniform, so the requested accuracy is reached.

Every operation at a finite refinement is Borel measurable in the pilot frequencies: Gaussian rectangle probabilities are continuous in a positive-definite covariance, finite sums and finite linear programs with lexicographic tie-breaking are Borel maps, and a terminating adaptive calculation is measurable because each halt set is Borel and there are countably many refinement levels.  The projection \(P_B\) is continuous and is the identity on \(\mathcal R_B\), so projected full-box nets cover the feasible design set.  These observations prove joint measurability of all cell values.  Retain exactly those children satisfying
\[
\widehat v_{n,j,b}
\le\min_c\widehat v_{n,j,c}+t_n,
\tag{21}
\]
where the minimum ranges only over nonempty feasible children of the selected parent, and choose the first retained child in the stipulated lexicographic order.  A minimizer of the finite list is always retained, so the selected feasible cells are nonempty and nested.  After depth \(k_n\), return the point obtained by successively minimizing the fixed ordered coordinates over the final compact feasible cell.  This point is unique by construction, belongs to \(\mathcal R_B\), and is a Borel function of the finite selected-cell index.  It is \(\widehat r_n\).

We prove the early-kill prefix property.  For a feasible child \(D_{j,b}\) of the exact population parent \(\mathcal D_{j-1}^\dagger\), put
\[
v_{j,b}=\min_{r\in\mathcal R_B\cap D_{j,b}}L(r),
\qquad E_j=\{b:v_{j,b}=V^*\},
\tag{22}
\]
where infeasible children are omitted.  The set \(E_j\) is nonempty because the closed children cover \(\mathcal D_{j-1}^\dagger\), and its feasible part contains a global minimizer by the definition of \(\mathcal D_{j-1}^\dagger\).  Continuity of \(L\), compactness of every feasible child, and finiteness of the child list imply
\[
\gamma_j(L)=
\begin{cases}
\min_{b\notin E_j}\{v_{j,b}-V^*\},&E_j\text{ is not the full feasible child set},\\
+\infty,&E_j\text{ is the full feasible child set}
\end{cases}
\quad\text{satisfies}\quad \gamma_j(L)>0.
\tag{23}
\]
By (19) and the deterministic numerical error, a fixed constant \(C_6\) may be chosen so that, on \(E_{n,C_v}\),
\[
\lvert\widehat v_{n,j,b}-v_{j,b}\rvert\le\alpha_n,
\qquad \alpha_n=C_6b_n,
\tag{24}
\]
simultaneously for every cell that can be tested through depth \(k_n\).  This simultaneity requires no growing-cell union bound because (19) is uniform on all of \(\mathcal R_B\) and the numerical error is deterministic.

Suppose the empirical parent at depth \(j-1\) is \(\mathcal D_{j-1}^\dagger\).  For every \(b\in E_j\), (24) and the fact that every child value is at least \(V^*\) give
\[
\widehat v_{n,j,b}-\min_c\widehat v_{n,j,c}\le2\alpha_n.
\tag{25}
\]
For every \(b\notin E_j\), comparison with any member of \(E_j\) gives
\[
\widehat v_{n,j,b}-\min_c\widehat v_{n,j,c}
\ge\gamma_j(L)-2\alpha_n.
\tag{26}
\]
Consequently, if
\[
2\alpha_n<t_n,
\qquad t_n+2\alpha_n<\gamma_j(L),
\tag{27}
\]
then (21) retains every and only the children in \(E_j\).  The first retained child is exactly the first population-eligible child, namely \(\mathcal D_j^\dagger\).  This argument does not require an isolated minimizer.  If a minimizer is on a boundary shared by several children, each closed child containing it belongs separately to \(E_j\), each is retained by (25), and the same lexicographic rule is applied to that full tied list.  Disconnected or flat minimizing sets likewise only enlarge \(E_j\).  Induction over \(j\) proves prefix stabilization whenever (27) holds at every preceding depth.

Define the deterministic analysis depth
\[
j_n(L)=\max\left(\{0\}\cup
\left\{j\le k_n:t_n+2\alpha_n<
\min_{1\le i\le j}\gamma_i(L)\right\}\right).
\tag{28}
\]
Because \(\alpha_n=o(t_n)\), the first inequality in (27) holds eventually.  For every fixed \(j\), the finite minimum of \(\gamma_1(L),\ldots,\gamma_j(L)\) is positive, whereas \(t_n+2\alpha_n\to0\) and \(k_n\to\infty\).  Therefore
\[
j_n(L)\longrightarrow\infty.
\tag{29}
\]
For represented inputs, the certified theorem applied to each restricted cell gives outward intervals \([\underline v_{j,b,s},\overline v_{j,b,s}]\) and \([\underline V_s,\overline V_s]\), with widths tending to zero as the refinement index \(s\) increases.  Whenever \(b\notin E_j\),
\[
v_{j,b}-V^*>0
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\underline v_{j,b,s}-\overline V_s>0
\quad\text{for all sufficiently large }s.
\tag{30}
\]
Taking the minimum of these finitely many positive outward lower differences certifies the positive term in (23).  Thus (28) is precisely the asserted depth envelope derived from the certified prefix-separation profile; the selector itself does not need to know the stopping depth (28).

Set
\[
a_n(L)=\sup_{m\ge n}2^{-j_m(L)}.
\tag{31}
\]
This sequence is deterministic, nonincreasing, and tends to zero by (29).  On \(E_{n,C_v}\), induction using (25)--(28) places both \(\widehat r_n\) and \(r^\dagger\) in \(\mathcal C_{j_n(L)}^\dagger\), even if the empirical path diverges after that depth.  The stipulated cell-diameter bound gives
\[
\lVert\widehat r_n-r^\dagger\rVert_2
\le\sqrt{2K}(1-\rho)2^{-j_n(L)}
\le\sqrt{2K}(1-\rho)a_n(L).
\tag{32}
\]
Together with (9), this proves the locally uniform \(O_P\{a_n(L)\}\) assertion.  Given a fixed depth \(k\), (29) implies \(j_n(L)\ge k\) eventually; the same induction proves simultaneous equality of every selected box and feasible cell through depth \(k\), uniformly over the fixed bounded nuisance fiber.

It remains to couple this design to a decision rule.  At deterministic refinement level \(s\), use a fixed finite state net, a fixed truncation rectangle partitioned into disjoint half-open rational rectangles, the Gaussian probability enclosures, and the finite primal--dual game in \(\mathrm{thm:certified\text{-}computation}\).  Let its total state, tail, quadrature, rounding, and game error be \(\xi_s\downarrow0\), and let \(J_s<\infty\) be its number of inside rectangles.  Resolve all finite ties lexicographically and use one fixed action outside the truncation rectangle.  A deterministic block-diagonal choice \(s_n\uparrow\infty\) can be made so slowly that
\[
\xi_{s_n}\longrightarrow0,
\qquad \frac{J_{s_n}}{\sqrt n}\longrightarrow0.
\tag{33}
\]
For instance, after choosing level \(s\), keep it until both inequalities with bounds \(1/s\) hold.  The resulting pilot-dependent rectangle-constant rule \(\delta_n\) is jointly measurable by the finite Borel construction already used for the cell values.

We verify its risk rather than invoking an unspecified central limit theorem.  Let \(\beta_n=\beta(q_n(h,v))\), let \(u_n=\beta_n-\widehat\beta\), and, conditional on \(\mathscr P_n\), define the \(2K\)-vector
\[
H_{i,ax}=\frac{\mathbf 1\{X_i=x,A_i=a,R_i=1\}}
{p_xe_{ax}\widehat r_{n,ax}}
(Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}-\widehat\beta_{ax}).
\tag{34}
\]
Here the product in (34) is interpreted only on \(R_i=1\), where \(Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}=Y_i\).  Annotation ignorability gives
\[
E(H_i\mid\mathscr P_n)=u_n.
\tag{35}
\]
For distinct cells the coordinate products in \(H_iH_i^\top\) vanish.  Hence direct conditional calculation gives
\[
\operatorname{Var}(H_i\mid\mathscr P_n)
=\operatorname{diag}_{a,x}\left\{
\frac{\sigma_{n,ax}^2+u_{n,ax}^2}
{p_xe_{ax}\widehat r_{n,ax}}
\right\}-u_nu_n^\top,
\tag{36}
\]
where \(\sigma_{n,ax}^2=\sigma_{ax}^2(q_n(h,v))\).  Consequently the exact conditional covariance of \(\sqrt n(\widetilde\theta_n-\theta_p(q_n(h,v)))\) is
\[
S_n=A_{\mathrm{map}}\left[
\operatorname{diag}_{a,x}\left\{
\frac{\sigma_{n,ax}^2+u_{n,ax}^2}
{p_xe_{ax}\widehat r_{n,ax}}
\right\}-u_nu_n^\top\right]A_{\mathrm{map}}^\top.
\tag{37}
\]
The additional matrix
\[
\operatorname{diag}_{a,x}\left\{
\frac{u_{n,ax}^2}{p_xe_{ax}\widehat r_{n,ax}}
\right\}-u_nu_n^\top
\tag{38}
\]
is positive semidefinite because it is the covariance of the vector whose \((a,x)\)-coordinate is \(\mathbf 1\{X=x,A=a,R=1\}u_{n,ax}/(p_xe_{ax}\widehat r_{n,ax})\).  Equations (12), (13), and the finite-support variance formula give, locally uniformly,
\[
\lVert S_n-\widehat\Sigma_n(\widehat r_n)\rVert_F=o_P(1).
\tag{39}
\]
Indeed, the leading variance difference is \(O_P(b_n)\), while (38) is \(O_P(b_n^2)\).  Equations (3), (4), and (38) give a deterministic positive lower eigenvalue for \(S_n\) with probability tending to one uniformly on the bounded fiber.

The defining AIPW equation and (35) give the exact sum representation
\[
\sqrt n\{\widetilde\theta_n-\theta_p(q_n(h,v))\}
=\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^nA_{\mathrm{map}}(H_i-u_n).
\tag{40}
\]
Conditional on \(\mathscr P_n\), these summands are independent and centered.  They are uniformly bounded before the factor \(n^{-1/2}\), because \(\lvert Y\rvert\le C_Y\), \(\widehat\beta\) lies in the convex hull of \(\mathcal Y\), and
\[
p_xe_{ax}\widehat r_{n,ax}
\ge\rho\min_{x,a}p_xe_{ax}>0.
\tag{41}
\]
On the positive-eigenvalue event for \(S_n\), normalize (40) by \(S_n^{-1/2}\).  The normalized array has identity summed covariance, and the sum of its third Euclidean absolute moments is at most \(C_7n^{-1/2}\).  The convex-set bound \(\mathrm{lem:bentkus\text{-}convex\text{-}set}\) therefore gives, for every convex Borel set \(C\),
\[
\left|P\{\sqrt n\,\widetilde\theta_n\in C\mid\mathscr P_n\}
-P\{G_n\in C\mid\mathscr P_n\}\right|
\le400d^{1/4}C_7n^{-1/2},
\qquad G_n\sim N(h,S_n).
\tag{42}
\]
Here \(\sqrt n\,\theta_p(q_n(h,v))=h\) follows from \(\mathrm{thm:local\text{-}chart\text{-}membership}\).  Every half-open rectangle in the rule is convex and Borel.  Summing (42) over its \(J_{s_n}\) inside rectangles, and controlling the single outside action by the sum of the inside probability differences, bounds the conditional data-to-\(N(h,S_n)\) risk error by
\[
2R_HJ_{s_n}\,400d^{1/4}C_7n^{-1/2}=o(1)
\tag{43}
\]
uniformly on the bounded fiber, by (33).

Apply (17) with (39).  Since the loss is bounded by \(R_H\), replacing \(N(h,S_n)\) by \(N\{h,\widehat\Sigma_n(\widehat r_n)\}\) changes the conditional risk of the same possibly discontinuous rule by \(o_P(1)\), uniformly in \(h\) and bounded \(v\).  Boundedness and the uniform good-event probabilities convert (43) and this \(o_P(1)\) term into an unconditional \(o(1)\) risk difference.  By construction of the finite game,
\[
\sup_{h\in\mathcal H}
E_{N\{h,\widehat\Sigma_n(\widehat r_n)\}}
\left[\sum_{j=1}^M\delta_{n,j}(Z)\ell_{\mathrm{reg}}(h,j)\right]
\le\widehat L_n(\widehat r_n)+\xi_{s_n}.
\tag{44}
\]
Finally, (19), (32), the continuity modulus (17), and \(L(r^\dagger)=V^*\) imply
\[
\widehat L_n(\widehat r_n)
\le V^*+o_P(1).
\tag{45}
\]
Combining (43)--(45), using bounded loss on bad pilot events, and taking the supremum over the fixed bounded nuisance fiber proves both the asserted \(o(1)\) data-to-Gaussian risk transfer and
\[
\limsup_{n\to\infty}\ \sup_{h\in\mathcal H,\,\lVert v\rVert\le C_v}
E\!\left[\sum_{j=1}^{M}\delta_{n,j}(\sqrt n\,\widetilde\theta_n)
\ell_{\mathrm{reg}}(h,j)\right]\le V^*.
\tag{46}
\]

We close by stating exactly what can and cannot be concluded about a faster spatial rate.  For arbitrary \(\epsilon>0\), define continuous objectives on \([0,1]\) by
\[
f_+(z)=\epsilon z,
\qquad f_-(z)=\epsilon(1-z),
\qquad g(z)=\epsilon/2.
\tag{47}
\]
Their unique, hence canonical, minimizers are zero and one, and
\[
\lVert g-f_+\rVert_\infty
=\lVert g-f_-\rVert_\infty=\epsilon/2.
\tag{48}
\]
A selector receiving only the common approximation \(g\) and the error guarantee in (48) must return the same \(z_g\) in both cases, while
\[
\max\{\lvert z_g\rvert,\lvert z_g-1\rvert\}\ge\frac12.
\tag{49}
\]
Because \(\epsilon\downarrow0\) is arbitrary, continuity and uniform objective-approximation control alone furnish no objective-uniform spatial recovery modulus tending to zero.  The witness (47) is not shown to belong to the Gaussian-risk family \(r\mapsto L(r)\); accordingly, (49) establishes no model-specific impossibility and does not rule out a faster rate for a fixed Gaussian-risk law with an additional optimizer-identification modulus.
